0.why: VerticalTextModule.cpp:161 divides getVoltage() by 10 and adds it to the hue knob with no isConnected test and no channel loop; line 163 takes fmodf of the sum, and nanovg's nvgHSLA adds 1 to a negative hue, so the result wraps either way

1.why: VerticalTextModule.cpp:172 passes getVoltage() to a dsp::SchmittTrigger with its default thresholds, which fire at 1 and reset at 0

2.why: VerticalTextModule.cpp:156 multiplies getVoltage() by 5 only when the port is connected and line 159 adds it to the size knob, clamping the sum to 8 and 76

3.why: VerticalTextModule.cpp:187 adds 5 to getVoltage() and divides by 10, then line 189 multiplies the glow knob by that instead of adding, so the knob is a scale factor while a cable is in and the sole control while it is not

comment: Source read at commit a7468df, whose plugin.json is byte-identical to the installed one; src and res have not changed since a585095, so the three commits carrying version 2.0.0 are indistinguishable in behaviour anyway. The panel SVG holds no text elements, so nothing on this module is labelled and every line has to start from what the control does. Three faults worth knowing. The saturation knob is configured 0 to 2 but getCurrentColor hands the value to nvgHSL, which clamps saturation to 1, so the upper half of that knob's travel is a proved dead zone. dataFromJson at line 564 writes the saved saturation into the knob, and what dataToJson saved at line 524 is the effective saturation, which the clock input sets to 0 — so a patch saved in the desaturated state reopens with the knob itself on zero. The glow input multiplies its knob rather than adding to it, which is the usual surprise: a patched cable sitting at 0V halves the glow and one at -5V removes it, and the knob is dead as a level while the cable is in. The font knob's maximum is fontPaths.size() - 1, which would be -1 if the fonts folder were ever empty. The text field widget is added to the panel at -1000,-1000, which is why editing shows no box. All four inputs are read on channel 0 only and the module has no outputs and no lights.
